totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size

totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this returns 2 instead of 1, and for 100/50 it returns 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, the Next link stays enabled, and clicking it loads an empty page at offset == user_count. It should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (with the existing zero-count special case).
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. When the total equals the limit (an exact multiple), pagination allows navigating to an empty page at offset == user_count and shows something like 2/2 with no members. The candidate pins the cause on the totalPages calculation and the golden points to the next-action capping, but the symptom and underlying problem are the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The remove_member test uses xhr :put to call the remove_member action, but the route defines delete 'members' => 'groups#remove_member' requiring DELETE method.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
remove_member automatic-group spec uses the wrong HTTP verb

The 'cannot remove members from automatic groups' example calls xhr :put, :remove_member, but the route added in config/routes.rb is DELETE /admin/groups/:group_id/members (and the other remove_member example correctly uses :delete). Controller specs dispatch by action name and bypass routing, so this test would still pass even if the DELETE route were missing or mapped to the wrong action, and it misdocuments the API contract.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the remove_member test using xhr :put even though the route is defined as DELETE. This is the same HTTP verb mismatch.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `totalPages` calculation using `Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1` produces an extra page when `user_count` is an exact multiple of `limit`, leading to incorrect pagination. For example, with 100 users and a limit of 50, it reports 3 pages instead of 2, allowing navigation to an empty page.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
totalPages is off by one when member count is an exact multiple of the page size

totalPages computes Math.floor(user_count / limit) + 1. For user_count=50 and limit=50 this returns 2 instead of 1, and for 100/50 it returns 3 instead of 2. showingLast therefore stays false on the real last page, the Next link stays enabled, and clicking it loads an empty page at offset == user_count. It should use Math.ceil(user_count / limit) (with the existing zero-count special case).
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same bug: the Math.floor(user_count/limit)+1 totalPages calculation adds an extra page when user_count is an exact multiple of limit, which lets the user navigate to an empty page.

false_positives.candidate:
Public group members page now silently truncates to the first 50 members with no way to reach the rest

The members endpoint now defaults to limit=50 and Group#findMembers always sends limit=50, but this same endpoint/model is used by the public discourse/routes/group-members route and templates/group/members.hbs, which have no pagination controls at all (pagination was only added to the admin template). Previously non-automatic groups returned all members and automatic groups up to 200. Now any group with more than 50 members only ever displays the first 50 alphabetically on its public members page.

Members endpoint accepts unbounded and negative limit/offset

limit and offset are taken from params with only to_i and no clamping. A caller who can view a group can pass limit=1000000 to force counting/serializing the entire membership in one request (automatic groups were previously capped at 200), or a negative limit/offset to trigger a database error and a 500. Clamp limit to a sane range (e.g. 1..200) and offset to >= 0.

Group update silently hides the group when the visible parameter is omitted

update guards alias_level with present? and name with an explicit nil check, but assigns group.visible = params[:visible] == "true" unconditionally. Any PUT/PATCH that updates only some fields (for example a rename or alias change from another API client, or the legacy PATCH membership call whose handling was removed) will force visible to false and return success, silently hiding the group. Only assign visible when the parameter is present.

Creating a group discards the alias_level chosen in the form

The admin form always shows the alias_level combo box and Group#asJSON sends alias_level on create, but the new create action only assigns name and visible. A group created with a non-default alias level is saved with the default 0 while the in-memory Ember object still shows the chosen value, so the setting appears applied until the page is reloaded. Assign params[:alias_level] in create as update does.

Stale usernames input leaks between group edit pages

AdminGroupController is a singleton and its new plain `usernames` property is never reset; setupController only sets the model and loads members. Text typed into the Add Members selector for one group is still bound and visible when the admin opens a different group, and clicking Add there would submit the previous group's usernames to the new group. Clear controller usernames (and stale paging state) in setupController or after a successful add.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The findMembers() call is now asynchronous and unhandled. The controller may not have member data immediately available, creating a race condition.
Expected to return a value at the end of function - code paths without explicit returns will return undefined

The route provides the group's ID in params[:id], but the code attempts to read it from params[:group_id], causing the action to fail. This results in a broken feature when trying to access group memberships.

true_positives.golden_comment: BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Validation has a write side effect and counts one signup attempt multiple times

EmailValidator.validate_each calls BlockedEmail.should_block?, which increments match_count and saves the BlockedEmail row. Validation is not a single commit-time event: UsersController#create calls user.valid? and then user.save, and save validates again, so one blocked signup attempt increments the counter twice. Any other valid? check, or a save that ultimately fails for an unrelated reason such as the password, also records a match even though no account attempt completed. Separate the pure blocked check from hit recording, or record the hit only once at the point an attempt is actually rejected.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point out that the blocked-email check method has write side effects: it updates match statistics during what should be a read or check. The candidate stresses double counting rather than race conditions, but the underlying issue is the same.

true_positives.golden_comment: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Blocked-email lookup can be bypassed by changing email case

BlockedEmail.should_block? performs an exact where(email: email) lookup using the raw user-supplied value, and neither BlockedEmail nor EmailValidator downcases or strips the address before storage or lookup; User.new_from_params also assigns the submitted email unchanged. PostgreSQL string comparison and the unique index are case-sensitive, so an address blocked as bad@spam.example can register as Bad@SPAM.example, and BlockedEmail rows differing only by case can coexist. Normalize the email (for example with Email.downcase and strip) both when creating BlockedEmail records and when checking them.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same problem: the lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? is case-sensitive, so a blocked address can get past the block by changing letter case.

false_positives.candidate:
match_count increment is a non-atomic read-modify-write

should_block? loads the BlockedEmail row, does record.match_count += 1 in memory, and saves it. Two concurrent attempts with the same blocked email can both read the same count and both write count+1, losing one hit; the full-row save can also overwrite concurrent changes to the record. Use an atomic database increment such as update_all("match_count = match_count + 1, last_match_at = ...") or increment_counter instead.

rejectedEmails is shared mutable state on the controller prototype

rejectedEmails is initialized as Em.A([]) in the class definition passed to extend(). In Ember, mutable array/object values declared this way live on the prototype and are shared rather than copied per instance, and createAccount mutates that array with pushObject while nothing ever clears it. Rejected addresses can therefore leak across controller instances and remain rejected for the lifetime of the app/session instead of being scoped to one account-creation flow. Initialize the array per instance (for example in init) and reset it when the create-account modal is shown or closed.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.

true_positives.golden_comment: -ms-align-items never existed in any version of IE/Edge; the correct legacy property is -ms-flex-align.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
align-items() has incomplete and invalid legacy vendor mappings

flexbox() and inline-flex() emit -moz-box/-moz-inline-box displays, but align-items() provides no -moz-box-align, so alignment is ignored by the legacy Mozilla box implementation for the header centering, .small-action centering, and bullet-badge baseline alignment. The block also emits the non-existent -ms-align-items property at line 121 while the actual IE10 property is -ms-flex-align, so that line is dead code and does not provide the intended support.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says outright that -ms-align-items doesn't exist and that the correct IE10 property is -ms-flex-align. That is the same issue as the golden comment. The candidate also raises a separate point about a missing -moz-box-align, but this extra content does not change the match.

true_positives.golden_comment: -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group require values starting from 1, not 0. If $val is 0, this will cause incorrect rendering in older browsers, leading to layout issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
order() mistranslates flex order for legacy WebKit/Mozilla box layout

The order() mixin copies the same value to order and to -webkit-box-ordinal-group/-moz-box-ordinal-group, but the legacy ordinal-group properties are 1-based and unordered items default to group 1, whereas flex order is 0-based and unordered items default to 0. Thus order(0) is invalid for legacy box layout and order(1) collides with unordered items there while following them in modern flex layout; the legacy properties need $val + 1 to preserve the same ordering.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same problem. The legacy ordinal-group properties are 1-based, so passing 0 straight through from the order() mixin is invalid and breaks layout in older browsers. The candidate goes further and proposes $val + 1 as the fix, but the core issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
Right-floated small-action button loses alignment in new flex container

.small-action is made a flex container at lines 264-265, but its direct-child button still relies on float: right at line 309. Floats do not apply to flex items, and no margin-left: auto, justify-content, or equivalent replacement is added, so the button will sit immediately after .small-action-desc instead of at the right edge of the row.

extra-info-wrapper becomes a flex item without shrink/truncation constraints

Adding order(2) makes .extra-info-wrapper participate as a flex item between the header title and the order(3) panel in the new .d-header .contents flex container, but it gets no flex sizing, min-width: 0, overflow, or truncation rules. A long topic title with category badges therefore cannot shrink below its content size and can push or compress the panel, causing the header controls to overflow or be clipped on narrow widths instead of the topic info truncating.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Mixing float: left with flexbox causes layout issues. Further this PR removes the float-based right alignment for .d-header .panel, which may cause the login panel in the non-Ember/noscript header (where .panel is nested inside .row and not a flex item) to stack under the title instead of remaining right-aligned.

true_positives.golden_comment: The include_website_name method is missing the required ? suffix. Rails serializers expect include_ methods to end with ? for conditional attribute inclusion, a convention followed by other methods in this serializer. Without it, the website_name attribute may not be conditionally included as intended. Additionally, the '.' << website_host string concatenation should be replaced with '.' + website_host or '.#{website_host}' to avoid mutating string literals, which can lead to issues.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
website_name include predicate is misnamed and bypasses untrusted-user hiding

The conditional is defined as include_website_name instead of the include_website_name? convention used by ActiveModel Serializers and by the other predicates in this file, so it is never invoked and website_name is always serialized. Additionally, :website_name is absent from untrusted_attributes, which hides :website for TL0 users viewed anonymously. Anonymous visitors therefore receive the host and path derived from a website that was intended to be hidden, and profiles without a website also gain a spurious website_name: nil key.
true_positives.reasoning: Both identify that include_website_name is missing the ? suffix, which breaks the ActiveModel Serializers convention used elsewhere in the file. Because of this, the conditional inclusion does not work. The candidate does not mention the string mutation point, but the main issue matches.

false_positives.candidate:
Same-domain check is asymmetric for apex and www hosts

When the website is http://www.example.com/me and the instance is example.com, the hosts have different label counts, so execution reaches the final branch, which only checks whether the instance host ends with the website host. That check fails and only www.example.com is shown. The reverse configuration, website example.com/me on instance www.example.com, does return example.com/me. The common apex/www combination is therefore handled inconsistently and the requested full path is not shown.

Stripping the first host label falsely matches domains under public suffixes

The sibling-subdomain branch assumes the registrable domain is always the last two labels. For example, website example.co.uk/user and an unrelated instance at other.co.uk both reduce to co.uk after removing the first label, so the serializer incorrectly displays example.co.uk/user as though the website belonged to the instance domain. The same false positive applies to other multi-part public suffixes and shared suffixes such as github.io.

Displayed website text drops query string and fragment

For a matching domain the display text is built from URI#path only. A website such as http://example.com/user?tab=posts#details is displayed as example.com/user even though the actual link points to the full URL, so the supposedly complete URL shown to readers is truncated and can misrepresent the destination, particularly for URLs whose identity is in the query string.

New website_name branches and visibility rules are untested

The added examples cover only an unrelated two-label domain, an exact host match, and a website that is the parent of the instance host. They do not exercise the equal-length sibling-subdomain branch, the apex-versus-www case, a blank or malformed website, or serialization of website_name for a TL0 user viewed anonymously; the untrusted_attributes list in the TL0 context is also unchanged. The untested include predicate and subdomain logic can therefore regress, or leak the hidden website, without any spec failing.

true_positives.golden_comment: The TopicEmbed.import method is susceptible to a NoMethodError if the contents parameter is nil when attempting to append a string, and an XSS vulnerability due to unescaped url interpolation in the generated HTML.
true_positives.matched_candidate: Embed URL is interpolated unescaped into raw HTML TopicEmbed.import appends "#{url}" to the post body without HTML-escaping or URL-encoding url. Because the resulting post uses raw_html rendering, a feed- or import-supplied URL containing a single quote can break out of the href attribute and inject additional attributes or markup, for example an onclick handler. The URL must be escaped before it is embedded in the generated footer HTML.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment raises two issues: a NoMethodError on nil contents, and XSS from unescaped url interpolation. The candidate identifies the XSS issue precisely, in the same method and the same interpolation. It misses the nil issue, but it does match a core part of the golden comment.

true_positives.golden_comment: Calling `i.content.scrub` assumes that `i.content` is always populated. However, many RSS feeds do not provide a `content` field, leading to a potential nil pointer exception when `i.content` is nil. A fallback to `description` should be implemented to prevent crashes.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
PollFeed crashes on feed items without a content field

The job unconditionally calls i.content.scrub. RSS items commonly provide only description/summary rather than content, in which case i.content is nil and this raises NoMethodError. The exception aborts processing of all remaining items, and because the scheduled job is configured with retry: false, a single such item can prevent every later valid feed entry from being imported on each poll.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same issue: calling i.content.scrub when content is nil, which raises NoMethodError on RSS items that only provide a description. The candidate adds detail about the consequences, but the underlying bug is identical.

false_positives.candidate:
Unsanitized feed HTML is stored and rendered as raw HTML

PollFeed passes CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub) directly to TopicEmbed.import without sanitizing it. TopicEmbed.import creates the post with cook_method raw_html, and Post#cook returns raw verbatim for that method, so feed-supplied markup such as script elements or event-handler attributes becomes the post's cooked HTML and is rendered to forum visitors. A malicious or compromised RSS/Atom feed can therefore achieve stored XSS in users' browsers, including administrators.

Embed controller spec expects the old synchronous retriever flow

This spec expects TopicRetriever.new(...).retrieve to be called, but EmbedController#best now calls Jobs.enqueue(:retrieve_topic, user_id: ..., embed_url: ...). The mocha expectation will therefore fail, and depending on test job settings the enqueued job may also run for real. The spec should expect Jobs.enqueue with :retrieve_topic and the correct arguments instead.

TopicEmbed.import has a check-then-create race on embed_url

Import first queries TopicEmbed.where(embed_url: url) and only creates the embed record if none exists, but concurrent PollFeed and RetrieveTopic jobs (the latter bypasses throttling for staff) can both observe no record for the same new URL and both create a topic/post. The unique database index on embed_url then makes one TopicEmbed.create! raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique, failing that job and rolling back its work. The creation path needs to handle the uniqueness conflict or serialize creation per URL.

Retrieval throttle key can be left without an expiry

retrieved_recently? sets the Redis throttle key with setnx and only afterwards calls expire as a separate command. If the process crashes or Redis errors between the two commands, the key persists forever with no TTL, permanently blocking retrieval for that embed URL and leaving visitors on the loading page. The key should be created atomically with its 60-second expiry.

Disqus import now depends on the original site being reachable

The import previously created the topic locally from the Disqus export, but now calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], ...), which fetches t[:link] over HTTP. If a thread's link is missing, malformed, or the original article is offline, open() raises or TopicEmbed.import returns nil and that thread's Disqus comments are skipped or the whole import aborts, losing data that is fully present in the export file. The removed --category option also means existing import invocations using it will fail and imported topics can no longer be placed in a category.

absolutize_urls mishandles common relative URL forms

Only href/src values beginning with '/' are rewritten. Plain relative references such as images/photo.jpg are left relative and will resolve against the Discourse host, producing broken links/images, while protocol-relative references such as //cdn.example.com/photo.jpg are incorrectly rewritten onto the source origin as http://source.example.com//cdn.example.com/photo.jpg. URL resolution should use URI joining against the source URL instead of string prefix checks.

Unauthenticated clients can flood retrieval with non-canonical URLs

Any client that spoofs the Referer header (the only embeddable-host check is that header, trivially set by non-browser clients) can call embed/best with arbitrary distinct URLs on the embeddable host, and every miss enqueues a RetrieveTopic job. The only throttling is per exact URL string inside the job and TopicEmbed is keyed by the exact URL string, so adding random query parameters, fragments, or other variants of the same article bypasses the throttle, floods the job queue with server-side fetches of the remote host, and can create duplicate topics for the same article. Retrieval needs canonical URL handling and a global/origin rate limit before enqueueing.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The PollFeed job calls open(SiteSetting.feed_polling_url) without validating the URL, allowing an attacker who controls the feed_polling_url site setting to make the server fetch arbitrary internal or external URLs.
The current origin validation using indexOf is insufficient and can be bypassed. An attacker could use a malicious domain like evil-discourseUrl.com to pass this check.
postMessage targetOrigin should be the origin (scheme+host+port), not the full referrer URL; using the full URL will cause the message to be dropped and prevent resizing.

The code sets X-Frame-Options: ALLOWALL which completely disables clickjacking protection. The referer validation can be bypassed (referer headers are easily spoofed), and the fallback to empty string for nil referer masks validation failures.
The ERB block closes with end if, which is invalid Ruby/ERB and will raise at render; it should just be end to close the if block.

An unescaped request header (request.referer) is interpolated into JavaScript without proper escaping, which can lead to XSS vulnerabilities if the referer contains malicious content. This issue can allow attackers to execute arbitrary scripts in the context of the application.

true_positives.golden_comment: The downsize method is defined twice. The second definition, which expects a single dimensions string parameter, overrides the first, which expected separate max_width and max_height parameters. This makes the original method unreachable and breaks existing code that calls it with separate width and height arguments.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Second downsize definition overrides the width/height version

Ruby replaces a method when it is defined again, so the three-argument downsize defined here makes the width/height downsize at line 145 dead code. Any existing caller passing from, to, width, and height will now raise ArgumentError instead of resizing, breaking the previous public API. The two signatures need to be merged or given different names.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the duplicate downsize definition, where the second (dimensions string) version overrides the width/height version. Both say this breaks existing callers that pass separate width and height arguments.

true_positives.golden_comment: Hardcoding maxSizeKB = 10 * 1024 ignores Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so the client-side limit can diverge from server-side and per-type settings (also applies to the 413 handler below).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Client validation hard-codes 10 MB for every upload type

validateUploadedFile receives a type but no longer uses Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'], so image and attachment limits are both replaced by 10 MB. Administrators with smaller limits get avoidable large uploads and server-side rejections, administrators with larger limits get incorrect client-side rejections, and the 413 handler at line 246 similarly reports 10 MB regardless of the configured limit.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments say the 10 MB limit is hard-coded and that the per-type site setting is ignored. Both note the client and server limits can diverge, and both mention that the 413 handler has the same problem.

true_positives.golden_comment: Passing 80% as the dimensions can fail for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, since the animated path uses gifsicle --resize-fit which expects WxH geometry, not a percentage; downsizing would then silently fail.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Percentage downsizing does not work correctly for animated GIFs

This passes the dimension string "80%" while forwarding SiteSetting.allow_animated_thumbnails. For an animated GIF, OptimizedImage dispatches to the gifsicle path, whose --resize-fit option expects pixel geometry such as 800x600 rather than a percentage, so the command can fail or produce an unintended size. When animated thumbnails are disabled, the ordinary ImageMagick path reads only frame [0], silently flattening an uploaded animated GIF based on a thumbnail preference rather than preserving the original animation.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate identifies the same problem as the golden comment. The '80%' dimension string is passed to gifsicle's --resize-fit for animated GIFs when allow_animated_thumbnails is true, and --resize-fit expects WxH geometry, so the command fails. The candidate's extra point about flattening animation when the setting is disabled is additional and does not change the match.

false_positives.candidate:
Failed in-place downsizing can corrupt the uploaded file

The same tempfile path is used as both conversion source and destination, and the boolean result of OptimizedImage.downsize is ignored. If conversion or ImageOptim fails, the loop retries up to five times against a file that may have been partially overwritten and then line 72 uploads whatever bytes remain, instead of retaining the original file or returning a clean error. Conversion should write to a separate temporary file and replace the upload only after success.

Remote-download limit ignores the configured maximum size

API URL downloads are now always capped at a hard-coded 10 megabytes instead of SiteSetting.max_image_size_kb. Sites that configured a lower limit will have the server fetch, store temporarily, and process files beyond their policy, while sites that configured a higher limit are incorrectly capped; the new image-only downsizer also does not make oversized non-image downloads conform to the relevant attachment limit.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The loop checking `tempfile.size` may never terminate correctly due to stale cached size, leading to potential infinite loops or incorrect file handling after modifications.

true_positives.golden_comment: logic: Potential nil pointer exception - if no TopicUser record exists, tu will be nil and calling methods on it will crash
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unsubscribe crashes when the user has no TopicUser record

TopicUser.find_by can return nil, for example when a logged-in user opens an unsubscribe URL for a topic they have never visited, tracked, or been emailed about (such as a forwarded email link). The next lines call tu.notification_level and tu.save! without a nil check, raising NoMethodError and returning a 500 instead of creating a muted/regular record for that user and topic.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: TopicUser.find_by can return nil when no record exists, and calling methods on tu then raises a nil error that crashes the unsubscribe action.

false_positives.candidate:
State-changing unsubscribe is performed by an unauthenticated-token GET request

The unsubscribe action mutates notification_level on a plain GET with only the session cookie for authorization and no CSRF token or signed unsubscribe key. Any third-party page, forum post, email link scanner, or browser prefetcher that causes the victim's browser to request /t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe will silently change the victim's notification setting. The mutation is also not idempotent: each repeated visit steps the level down again (watching/tracking to regular on the first visit, then regular to muted on a refresh or second visit), so prefetching, reloading the confirmation page, or revisiting the link produces a different result from the first click and can undo a level the user just re-selected on that page.

Unsubscribe bypasses the established TopicUser.change mechanism

set_notifications and other notification-level changes go through TopicUser.change, which stamps notifications_changed_at, sets notifications_reason_id to user_changed, creates the row if missing, and publishes a MessageBus notification_level_change so live clients update. This action instead assigns tu.notification_level directly and calls save!, so the change is recorded with a stale reason/timestamp and already-open clients and topic tracking state are never notified of the new level.

unsubscribe_link translation now requires an unsubscribe_url that MessageBuilder does not guarantee

config/locales/server.en.yml now interpolates %{unsubscribe_url} into the shared unsubscribe_link string, and both html_part (line 67) and body (line 90) render that string whenever add_unsubscribe_link is true. MessageBuilder provides defaults for site_name, base_url, and user_preferences_url but not for unsubscribe_url, so any caller that sets add_unsubscribe_link without also passing the new, undocumented unsubscribe_url (as the previous message_builder spec did) will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument and fail to send the email. The builder should supply a fallback or only include the per-topic sentence when an unsubscribe_url is present.

New unsubscribe behavior has no effective test coverage

false_positives.candidate:
One failing SendGrid cancellation blocks all other cancellations

All reminders are cancelled sequentially inside a single try block, while the Prisma delete operations are only executed by the Promise.all after the loop. If client.request throws for one reminder (for example an invalid, expired, or already-cancelled batch), the catch is taken, none of the queued deletes run, and every later reminder in remindersToCancel is never even attempted. The same failing reminder will be retried first on the next cron run, so other reminders whose scheduled time falls within the next hour can still be dispatched by SendGrid.

Deferred-only cancellation misses reminders that are due imminently

For a scheduled email this function now only sets cancelled=true and never cancels with SendGrid immediately, regardless of how soon the reminder is due. Cancellation therefore depends entirely on the periodic scheduleEmailReminders cron running before the SendGrid sendAt time. If a booking is cancelled a few minutes before its reminder and the next cron run happens after that time, SendGrid will already have sent the email; the cron's initial deleteMany for past scheduledDate rows then just removes the DB record. The previous immediate-cancellation behaviour covered this last-minute case.

Reschedule path bypasses the deferred cancellation mechanism and loses failures

Rescheduling calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true), which immediately POSTs a SendGrid cancellation instead of setting cancelled=true. This reintroduces the exact SendGrid pending-cancellations cap (100) that this PR is meant to work around for rescheduled bookings. Worse, if that POST fails, deleteScheduledEmailReminder only logs the error and returns without deleting the row or setting cancelled, so the scheduleEmailReminders cron (which only looks for cancelled=true) will never retry and the reminder for the old booking time will still be sent.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

true_positives.golden_comment: The addGuests.handler.ts blacklist check uses blacklistedGuestEmails.includes(guest) after lowercasing the blacklist but not the input guest emails, allowing attackers to bypass BLACKLISTED_GUEST_EMAILS restrictions by submitting emails with uppercase characters.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not de-duplicate the request itself

uniqueGuests only removes guests that exactly match an existing attendee email and compares the raw guest string against a lower-cased blacklist. It does not lower-case guests or de-duplicate within the submitted array. A direct API call such as ['A@example.com', 'a@example.com'], or re-adding an existing attendee with different capitalization, can create duplicate attendee rows and duplicate invites, and a blacklisted address can bypass the blacklist by changing capitalization.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate says the raw guest string is compared against a lower-cased blacklist, so a blacklisted address can get past the check by changing its capitalization. That is the same bug the golden comment describes. The candidate also raises extra de-duplication problems, but those do not change the match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The logic for checking team admin/owner permissions is incorrect. This condition uses AND (&&) which requires both isTeamAdmin AND isTeamOwner to be true, but it should use OR (||) since a user needs to be either an admin OR an owner to have permission.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Team admin/owner authorization uses AND instead of OR

isTeamAdminOrOwner is computed as isTeamAdmin(...) && isTeamOwner(...), so a team admin who is not also the team owner fails the check. Such users are rejected with FORBIDDEN unless they are separately the organizer or an attendee, even though the variable name and intended permission indicate admin OR owner should be sufficient.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: the team admin/owner permission check combines isTeamAdmin and isTeamOwner with && when it should use ||.

true_positives.golden_comment: The sendAddGuestsEmails function in email-manager.ts passes the full calendarEvent.attendees array when determining which attendees receive AttendeeScheduledEmail vs AttendeeAddGuestsEmail, but checks if newGuests.includes(attendee.email) where newGuests is the input guests array.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Email sender receives the raw guest list instead of the filtered unique guest list

The handler filters duplicates/blacklisted addresses into uniqueGuests for the database write, but then calls sendAddGuestsEmails(evt, guests) with the original unfiltered input. Existing attendees who were correctly filtered out of the write are therefore classified as new guests by sendAddGuestsEmails and receive a fresh AttendeeScheduledEmail invitation instead of the guests-added notification.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug: sendAddGuestsEmails checks newGuests.includes(attendee.email) against the raw input guests array instead of the filtered uniqueGuests list. As a result, existing attendees can be misclassified as new guests and receive the wrong email. The golden comment frames this from the email-manager side and the candidate from the handler call side, but the underlying problem is identical.

true_positives.golden_comment: uniqueGuests filters out existing attendees and blacklisted emails but does not deduplicate duplicates within the input; createMany can insert duplicate attendee rows if the client submits repeated emails.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guest de-duplication and blacklist checks are case-sensitive and do not de-duplicate the request itself

uniqueGuests only removes guests that exactly match an existing attendee email and compares the raw guest string against a lower-cased blacklist. It does not lower-case guests or de-duplicate within the submitted array. A direct API call such as ['A@example.com', 'a@example.com'], or re-adding an existing attendee with different capitalization, can create duplicate attendee rows and duplicate invites, and a blacklisted address can bypass the blacklist by changing capitalization.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate explicitly says uniqueGuests does not de-duplicate within the submitted array, which can create duplicate attendee rows. This is the golden issue. The candidate also raises extra case-sensitivity points, but these do not change the match.

true_positives.golden_comment: The `sendAddGuestsEmails` function does not check the `disableStandardEmails` flags in the `EventType` metadata, which may result in sending emails to hosts/attendees even when standard emails are disabled for the event type.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Guests-added emails ignore disabled standard email settings

sendAddGuestsEmails unconditionally emails the organizer, team members, and all attendees and takes no eventTypeMetadata argument. Unlike the other booking-change senders in this file, it does not check eventTypeDisableHostEmail/eventTypeDisableAttendeeEmail, and the handler does not pass booking.eventType metadata. Event types configured to disable standard host/attendee emails will still send these emails.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same problem: sendAddGuestsEmails never checks the disableStandardEmails metadata (host/attendee disable flags). As a result, emails go out even when the event type has standard emails disabled.

false_positives.candidate:
Guests can be added to cancelled, rejected, pending, or past bookings

The handler never checks booking.status or booking.endTime before creating attendees, updating the calendar, and sending guests-added/scheduled emails with a CONFIRMED ICS. A direct API caller can therefore mutate a cancelled, rejected, unconfirmed, or already-ended booking and cause new calendar/email invitations to be sent for an event that is not an accepted upcoming booking.

Calendar update uses the caller's credentials instead of the booking organizer's

The handler explicitly authorizes non-organizers (team admins/owners and attendees), but then loads credentials with getUsersCredentials(ctx.user) and constructs EventManager from the caller. The calendar event and destination calendar belong to booking.user/organizer, so for those authorized non-organizer callers EventManager cannot use the organizer's calendar credential and the external calendar attendee update can silently fail while the database and emails succeed, leaving systems inconsistent. The booking organizer's credentials/user should be used.

Guest list has no maximum length

The input schema accepts an arbitrarily large guests array. The handler then creates all attendees, loads a translation per attendee, updates the calendar, and sends email to the organizer/team plus every attendee. Any authorized caller, including an attendee, can use this for large-scale email fan-out/resource consumption and send platform-generated meeting invitations to many arbitrary addresses; the server should enforce a reasonable cap.

MultiEmail imports the @calcom/ui barrel from inside the same package

MultiEmail lives in @calcom/ui but imports Button, EmailField, Icon, and Tooltip from the '@calcom/ui' barrel, while that barrel exports MultiEmailLazy which dynamically imports this file. This creates a self-referential import cycle and pulls the whole UI barrel into a component that was specifically made lazy, risking circular-chunk/undefined-import problems and defeating the intended code splitting. The component should import from relative component paths.

Dialog state is not reset when closed without Cancel

multiEmailValue and isInvalidEmail are only cleared by the explicit Cancel button or on mutation success. Closing the dialog through the dialog close affordance, Escape, or overlay only calls setIsOpenDialog, so previously typed emails and a stale validation error remain the next time the dialog is opened and can be submitted accidentally. Editing the emails also does not clear isInvalidEmail after the user fixes the input.

No tests cover the new addGuests mutation

This PR adds a new mutation with organizer/team-admin/team-owner/attendee authorization branches, duplicate and blacklist filtering, database writes, calendar updates, and email fan-out, but adds no handler or integration tests. Tests should cover at least outsider rejection, admin versus owner access, organizer/attendee access, duplicate/blacklisted guests, and non-accepted bookings so authorization and filtering regressions are caught.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Starting with an array containing an empty string may cause validation issues. Consider starting with an empty array [] and handling the empty state in the MultiEmail component instead.

true_positives.golden_comment: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code comparison rejects uppercase and whitespace-padded entry

Generated codes are lowercase hex (crypto.randomBytes(5).toString('hex')), but verification only strips '-' and does an exact indexOf match, with no trim() or case normalization; the disable endpoint repeats the same logic. A user who manually transcribes a saved code in uppercase, or pastes it with surrounding whitespace, is told the code is incorrect even though they supplied the right code. The supplied value should be normalized (trim, remove dashes, lowercase) before comparison in both verification paths.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same problem: backup codes are checked with an exact, case-sensitive indexOf match, so a user who enters uppercase hex is rejected. The candidate also raises whitespace handling, but its core point is the same as the golden comment's.

true_positives.golden_comment: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Backup-code consumption is not atomic, so one code can be reused concurrently

The code performs a read, indexOf check, and separate prisma.user.update() to null out the used code. Two parallel login requests with the same backup code can both read the original encrypted list, both find the code, and both authenticate before either update is visible. This violates the stated exactly-once property of backup codes; consumption needs an atomic/transactional compare-and-update or locking.
true_positives.reasoning: Both describe the same race condition: backup code consumption is non-atomic (read, check, then update), so concurrent requests can reuse a single backup code and break the one-time-use guarantee.

true_positives.golden_comment: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
resetState leaves backup codes, TOTP secret, and the download URL in memory

resetState() clears only the password, error message, and step. It does not clear backupCodes, secret, dataUri, or backupCodesUrl, and never revokes the Blob object URL containing all plaintext backup codes. The modal component stays mounted on the settings page, so the full set of recovery codes and the TOTP secret remain retrievable in component state and via the still-valid blob URL long after the backup-codes screen is closed.
true_positives.reasoning: The golden comment is about the backup codes object URL never being revoked, which leaks memory when the component unmounts. The candidate also says the Blob object URL is never revoked, though it ties this to resetState and frames it as a security/data-retention problem rather than a memory leak. Both point to the same missing revokeObjectURL on the backup codes URL, but the framing differs.

false_positives.candidate:
Backup code can bypass the password when combined with a dummy TOTP field

Password verification at the top of authorize() only runs when credentials.totpCode is absent, while this new branch runs whenever credentials.backupCode is present and never validates the supplied TOTP value. An attacker can call the public credentials endpoint directly with an email, any totpCode value, and a valid backup code, skipping password verification entirely. A backup code therefore becomes a single-factor credential instead of a replacement for only the authenticator factor.

Successful 2FA enablement is only reported to the parent from the backup-codes Close button

handleEnable() now replaces onEnable() with setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes), and the only remaining call to onEnable() is the footer Close button for that step. If the dialog is dismissed through its normal onOpenChange path (close control, Escape, or outside interaction) after the server has already enabled 2FA, the parent is never notified and keeps rendering 2FA as disabled until a reload, while the modal also remains on the stale backup-codes step when reopened.

Users who enabled 2FA before this feature can never obtain backup codes

The migration leaves backupCodes null for every existing 2FA user, and this setup endpoint is the only place in the PR that generates backup codes, but it rejects anyone with twoFactorEnabled=true with TwoFactorAlreadyEnabled. Those users are nevertheless offered the Lost access backup-code flow at login and when disabling 2FA, and will only receive MissingBackupCodes, despite the error copy telling them to generate codes in settings where no such action exists.

No test exercises actually logging in or disabling 2FA with a backup code

The added e2e coverage only checks that the backup-codes download has the right filename, that copy shows a toast, and that the dialog closes, with explicit TODOs for checking file contents and for login/disable backup-code tests. The security-critical new behavior - login with a correct backup code, rejection of a wrong code, single-use invalidation of a consumed code, users with no stored codes, and disabling 2FA with a backup code - has no automated coverage, so regressions in these paths would ship undetected.

Password visibility toggle is removed from keyboard navigation for every PasswordField

Adding tabIndex={-1} to the show/hide password button in the shared PasswordField component makes that control unreachable by keyboard for all password fields across the app, not just in the 2FA modals touched by this PR. Keyboard and assistive-technology users can no longer toggle password visibility, an accessibility regression unrelated to backup codes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
Error message mentions 'backup code login' but this is a disable endpoint, not login

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic error: when externalCalendarId is provided, you're searching for a calendar where externalId === externalCalendarId, but this will always fail since you're looking for a calendar that matches itself. Should likely find by credentialId or use different logic.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Google updateEvent fallback can never find a calendar

When externalCalendarId is falsy, selectedCalendar is computed by finding a destination calendar whose externalId equals that same falsy externalCalendarId, which can never match a real calendar id, so selectedCalendar is undefined and calendar.events.update is called with calendarId: undefined. The previous behaviour fell back to the destination calendar's externalId. Legacy bookings and any update path without a stored externalCalendarId will therefore fail to update the Google event. The same dead fallback exists in deleteEvent, which then silently falls back to 'primary' and may delete from the wrong calendar.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments point to the same flawed lookup: the code finds a calendar whose externalId equals externalCalendarId, which is self-referential and can't work as a fallback. The golden comment frames the case as 'when provided' and the candidate as 'when falsy', but the bug and code location are the same: the fallback lookup can never yield a meaningful calendar.

true_positives.golden_comment: Logic inversion in organization creation: The slug property is now conditionally set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, instead of when it's false as originally intended. This change, combined with requestedSlug still being set when IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED is true, results in both properties being set when billing is enabled, and neither when disabled
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Unrelated inversion of organization slug assignment

This file is unrelated to destination calendars, but the change flips slug assignment from 'slug when team billing is NOT enabled' to 'slug only when team billing IS enabled' (and now sets both slug and requestedSlug in the billing case). Organizations created without team billing will be created without a slug, breaking their org URL/routing, while billing-enabled orgs get a final slug before the requested-slug flow expects it.
true_positives.reasoning: The candidate describes the same issue as the golden comment. The slug condition was inverted so it is now set when billing is enabled. As a result, both slug and requestedSlug are set when billing is enabled, and neither is set when it is disabled.

true_positives.golden_comment: The Calendar interface now requires createEvent(event, credentialId), but some implementations (e.g., Lark/Office365) still declare createEvent(event) only—this breaks the interface contract (also applies to other locations in the PR).
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Office365 createEvent ignores credentialId and always uses first host's calendar

EventManager now calls createEvent once per destination calendar with that host's credential, but this implementation does not accept/use credentialId and always targets destinationCalendar[0]. For a collective event, the second host's Office365 token is used to POST to /me/calendars/{first host's externalId}/events, which will 404 or create on the wrong calendar, so non-Google collective hosts do not actually receive their event despite the PR's goal. LarkCalendarService and the CalDAV BaseCalendarService have the identical first-element-only pattern.
true_positives.reasoning: Both point to the same thing: Office365, Lark and others don't accept the credentialId parameter in createEvent. The golden frames it as an interface contract violation. The candidate frames it as a functional bug, where credentialId is ignored and the first destination calendar is always used. Both identify the same code location, the same implementations, and the missing parameter.

false_positives.candidate:
Crash when Google Meet booking has no destination calendar

The code destructures the first element of evt.destinationCalendar and then accesses mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration without optional chaining or a null check. When destinationCalendar is null or an empty array (handleNewBooking explicitly sets it to null when neither the event type nor organizer has one), this throws a TypeError whenever evt.location is Google Meet, aborting EventManager.create instead of falling back to Cal Video as the previous optional-chained code did.

Secondary hosts' Google events use the main host's calendar as organizer email

createEvent always uses the first destination calendar's externalId as the organizer attendee email, even when credentialId identifies a different (secondary collective) host whose calendar is selected via the credentialId lookup below. The secondary host's event is therefore created on their calendar but attributed to the main host's calendar address, which Google can reject or display with the wrong organizer. The organizer email should come from the destination calendar matching the passed credentialId, not destinationCalendar[0]; updateEvent has the same defect.

Lark createEvent always uses the main host's calendar id

createEvent (and createAttendees) destructure only destinationCalendar[0] and ignore the credential being used. When EventManager iterates to the second collective host and instantiates Lark with that host's credential, it still creates the event and attendees on the first host's Lark calendar id, causing API failures or events on the wrong calendar. It needs the same per-credential destination selection Google received.

CalDAV createEvent filters by main host calendar for every host

BaseCalendarService.createEvent filters the credential's calendars to the first destination calendar's externalId. For a secondary collective host whose CalDAV account does not contain the main host's calendar, the filter yields zero calendars, Promise.all resolves empty, and the method still returns a fabricated uid as success, so EventManager records a booking reference for an event that was never created on the second host's calendar.

Video booking references lose their credentialId

referencesToCreate now sets credentialId to undefined for every non-calendar result, whereas previously video results kept result.credentialId. Dedicated video (e.g. Zoom/Daily) booking references are persisted without credentialId, and later flows such as handleCancelBooking only delete the video meeting when bookingVideoReference.credentialId is present, so video meetings for new bookings may leak/not be deleted or updated.

References created without externalId in fallback/other-calendar branches

In the branches where a destination has no credentialId, where no destination exists, and for the trailing other_calendar credentials (lines 380, 391, 403), createEvent is called without destination.externalId, so CalendarManager returns externalId undefined and the persisted BookingReference has externalCalendarId undefined. Previously references derived externalCalendarId from evt.destinationCalendar. Updates/deletes for those events then depend on the broken per-service fallbacks and can target 'primary' or no calendar instead of the calendar the event was created on.

Reschedule merge deletes only the first old calendar event

updateAllCalendarEvents now loops over all calendar references for updates, but the newBookingId cleanup still uses booking.references.find(...) and deletes only the first old calendar event. For a collective booking with one reference per host, the other hosts' old events are never deleted when merging into the new booking, leaving orphaned duplicate events on those hosts' calendars after reschedule.

Recurring cancellation duplicates deletes with wrong credentials

The new outer loop iterates every calendar reference, and inside the recurring/allRemainingBookings branch it again maps over all of the organizer's calendar credentials and, for each updated booking, picks only the first calendar reference via find(). Each recurring event is therefore delete-attempted once per reference times per credential, mostly with a credential that does not own that reference's uid/externalCalendarId. This produces spurious delete failures (and possible wrong-calendar deletions) for collective recurring bookings instead of deleting each reference once with its own credentialId.

Confirming a collective booking only creates the organizer's calendar event

The evt built for handleConfirmation contains only booking.destinationCalendar or the confirming user's destinationCalendar as a single-element array, with no destination calendars for the other collective hosts. Since EventManager.createAllCalendarEvents now creates events solely by iterating evt.destinationCalendar, a requires-confirmation collective booking that is later confirmed will only create an event for one host, defeating the multi-host fix on the confirmation path. The Stripe/PayPal webhook handlers build the same single-destination evt.

Collective team calendars are dropped when organizer has no destination calendar

evt.destinationCalendar is set to null when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar, and the collective merge then does evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...teamDestinationCalendars). With null, the optional chain silently no-ops, so all collected team hosts' destination calendars are lost and EventManager falls back to the first connected calendar instead of creating an event per host.

false_negatives.golden_comment: A null reference occurs in GoogleCalendarService.createEvent() and updateEvent() when mainHostDestinationCalendar is destructured from evt.destinationCalendar but evt.destinationCalendar is null or an empty array, causing mainHostDestinationCalendar to be undefined.
The optional chaining on mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration is redundant since you already check mainHostDestinationCalendar in the ternary condition.

The `credential` may be undefined when passed to `updateEvent` if `reference.credentialId` is set but the credential is not found. This can lead to a runtime error when `updateEvent` is called with an undefined credential, which should be handled to prevent crashes.

true_positives.golden_comment: The code uses forEach with async callbacks, which causes asynchronous operations (e.g., calendar/video event deletions, payment refunds) to run concurrently without being awaited. This 'fire-and-forget' behavior leads to unhandled promise rejections, race conditions, and incomplete cleanup, as surrounding try-catch blocks cannot properly handle errors from these unawaited promises. Replace forEach with for...of loops or Promise.all() with map() to ensure proper sequential execution and error handling.
true_positives.matched_candidate:
Async forEach leaves calendar/video deletion fire-and-forget

The forEach callback was made async to await getCalendar, but Array.prototype.forEach ignores the returned promises. Reschedule therefore proceeds to send the reschedule email and return true without waiting for calendar.deleteEvent or deleteMeeting to even start (the await on getCalendar defers them past the forEach), so in a request-scoped/serverless execution the old events can be left behind, and any rejection becomes an unhandled rejection that the surrounding try/catch cannot catch. Use `await Promise.all(bookingRefsFiltered.map(async ...))` or a for...of loop.
true_positives.reasoning: Both comments describe the same bug. An async forEach callback causes the calendar/video deletions to run fire-and-forget, so rejections go unhandled and escape the try/catch, and cleanup can be left incomplete. Both suggest the same fix: Promise.all with map, or a for...of loop.

false_positives.candidate:
Dynamic imports are started eagerly for every app

Every value in the appStore object literal is an import() call, so all 28 calls are evaluated as soon as this module is loaded. Code that needs only one app (for example getCalendar for a single credential) therefore still starts loading every calendar, video, CRM, and payment app and retains all of their side effects and memory/startup cost, defeating the intended per-app lazy loading. A rejected import for an app that is never used can also surface later as an unhandled rejection from the cached promise. Store thunks such as `applecalendar: () => import("./applecalendar")` and invoke the thunk at lookup time instead.

requestReschedule does not wait for old calendar/video deletion

bookingRefsFiltered.forEach now takes an async callback whose promise is discarded. Immediately afterwards the mutation sends the reschedule email and webhooks and returns, while the awaited getCalendar/deleteEvent and deleteMeeting work is still pending; it may be abandoned when the request ends and its failures are unhandled, leaving the supposedly cancelled calendar event and video meeting active. Await the deletions with Promise.all over map (or a for...of loop) before continuing.

Recurring-cancellation deletions can miss the later Promise.all entirely

For recurring bookings, calendar deletions are collected by pushing into apiDeletes from inside an async forEach callback that first awaits getCalendar and then awaits deleteEvent before pushing. The handler later awaits Promise.all(prismaPromises.concat(apiDeletes)), but concat snapshots apiDeletes at that moment, typically before those async callbacks have pushed anything. The handler can therefore delete the booking's attendees/references (losing the external uids needed to retry) and return while the external calendar deletions are not awaited or have not run, orphaning events on users' calendars. Collect the deletion promises synchronously via map/Promise.all or a sequential for...of and await them before the database cleanup completes.

false_negatives.golden_comment: Consider adding try-catch around the await to handle import failures gracefully
